notes: Math.random is the port's xorshift32 from 2463534242, reset before every chart.
A log axis' breaks: the ends as written (powStub), the gaps of intervalStub (log space).
anim: the break leaves of the axis' _axisGroup by anid after the settled first render (before) and at each sample after the action at T1.

cases.note: a log y axis, a break 50..900 '5%': in log space, the decades stepping over it
an absolute gap of 100: log(150) - log(50) in log space
two breaks, '3%' and 10: the lookup's second start overwrites the first end, which comes back as a power
min 100 inside the break 50..900: the break cut at the extent, its end tick the extent's
a line, the axis line and ticks shown, minor ticks and split lines
logBase 2 and a break 8..512
a log x axis under a scatter
a click on the log axis' break area expands it
a log y axis with a break under an inside dataZoom: two zooms change the extent, the lookup's first two entries follow it, the break ends come back through it
a log x axis with two breaks under an inside dataZoom (start / end values): the second start overwrites the first end in the lookup, the zoom rewrites only the extent's two
a break whose end is the nice extent's max (3000..10000, the data to 9000): the end tick and the extent's end are the one value through the lookup
a break whose start is the nice extent's min (1..20, the data from 2): the start and the extent's start are the one value
min and max written onto two breaks' outer ends (10..30 and 300..1000, min 10, max 1000)
the nice-end break under a dataZoom that brings the extent back onto it
a value singleAxis under a scatter, a break 20..80
a vertical singleAxis on the left, two breaks
a time singleAxis under a themeRiver, a break of a fortnight
a click on the single's break area expands it (singleAxisIndex)
expandAxisBreak and toggleAxisBreak by singleAxisIndex
an x value axis, labels turned 45: the break's two labels moved apart along the oriented boxes
a y value axis, labels turned 30
labels turned 90 on an x axis
an inverse x axis, labels turned -40
an inverse x axis turned -40, the break end's label far wider than its start's
an x axis turned 45, the break start's label far wider than its end's
a y axis turned 30, the break end's label far wider than its start's
an x axis turned -60, the break start's label far wider than its end's
turned 30 with a wide gap: the boxes meet the rect test but not the oriented one
a function formatter: the third argument carries the break of a break end
the break cut by min: the formatter is handed the clamped one
a log axis' formatter: the break as the lookup brings it back
triggerEvent: a click on a break label: params.break {start, end}; on a plain label none
triggerEvent on a value singleAxis: a plain label, then a break label (the break, and the break expands)
triggerEvent on a category singleAxis: the label of b (dataIndex 1)
no triggerEvent: a click on a break label is no event and expands nothing

anim.note: a dataZoom over a broken y axis: the break area moves from its old points to its new by anid
a dataZoom over a broken x axis: the area slides along it
a legend toggle: the area is drawn again where it was, no move
a second dataZoom while the first transition moves: the new one starts from the leaves as they are now
a second dataZoom on the broken x axis while the first moves: from the leaves as they are
a dataZoom back to the whole while the first one moves (100 ms in): back from where the leaves are
a legend toggle while a dataZoom moves: the render again keeps the leaves going from where they are
expandAxisBreak while a dataZoom moves: the area goes, the axis transition goes on
a third dataZoom while the second moves (each 150 ms after the last)

anchors: l-one-prct: a break end of each kind among the ticks
l-two: the first break's end comes back as a power, not 60
s-value: a break area on the single
s-click: the click expanded it by singleAxisIndex
p-formatter: a call with a break
p-event: the break label click carries the break
t-zoom: the area moves in between
t-zoom-twice: the second transition starts where the first one is (266 is its first frame) and leaves its path
s-value: the single's split lines are caught
